content.text: {"title":"The Library Parade Cart","premise":"In a little town library, Mayor Bramble announces that tonight’s parade must be the biggest ever. Mina, the child librarian, wants every reader to have a book to carry; Tuck the cart builder wants his new rolling cart admired; and Mayor Bramble wants a ridiculous, trumpet-blaring grand prize. One shared cart, a pile of books, a brass bell, and a red parade sash can turn the boast into three very different adventures.","cast_and_props":"Characters: Mina (child librarian; wants books matched with readers, initially believes the parade route is for townspeople), Tuck (cheerful cart builder; wants the cart to perform beautifully and be praised, initially believes Mayor Bramble will judge it), and Mayor Bramble (boastful mayor; wants the largest-looking parade and the golden megaphone prize, initially believes more noise means more success). Shared setting: the library, its front steps, and the short lane to the town square. Props: book cart, books, brass bell, red parade sash, golden megaphone prize, and a library cat named Button represented as a non-speaking physical entity if needed. Keep the cast at three speaking characters and the prop state small.","kernels_and_interactions":"1. Desire/assignment: Bramble issues a physical invitation for a biggest-parade contest; the red sash and golden megaphone make his goal concrete. 2. Knowledge and mistaken belief: Mina observes that several townspeople have borrowed books but are not coming to the square; Tuck hears only that the cart will be judged and misunderstands what counts as a successful parade; Bramble can learn that the library’s actual audience is elsewhere. 3. Cart performance: the cart can be decorated, pushed, rung, and loaded, but each choice changes its destination or usefulness rather than adding abstract score. 4. Sharing/ownership: Mina can hand books to readers, Tuck can transfer the cart’s sash or bell, and Bramble can give away or keep the golden megaphone. 5. Audience/meaning: the parade can become a noisy spectacle for the square, a rolling delivery to homebound readers, or a tiny procession led by books selected for specific people. Reuse scenes such as loading the cart, ringing the bell, and arguing over the route across all paths. The inciting action is Bramble tying the red sash to the cart and promising the golden megaphone to whoever creates the biggest parade; this establishes the conflict before anyone responds.","seed_parameters":"Seed 955885281 should choose initial conditions from scalar alternatives, not route numbers. Suggested premise keys: bramble.motive ('biggest' or 'useful'), mina.knows.audience_location (None, 'square', or 'homes'), tuck.belief.judge (None, 'mayor' or 'readers'), and cart.load_style ('tower' or 'matched'). Use the supplied seed to vary which fact is initially observed, which book bundle is available, and whether the brass bell is already attached. State keys should use existing entity prefixes, for example: bramble.motive, bramble.knows.mina_goal, mina.knows.audience_location, tuck.knows.judge, cart.owner, cart.location, cart.loaded, cart.load_style, cart.sash, cart.bell, books.bundle, books.delivered, mayor.prize, mayor.agreement, and parade.kind. Declare every slot first. Candidate selection should usually produce 5–10 events from 12–22 candidates, with one or two pivotal moments such as Mina choosing readers over the square or Bramble giving away the prize.","candidate_scenes":"Suggested 16 candidates: (1) 'tie_sash' bridge: Bramble ties the red sash to the cart and announces the prize. (2) 'hear_boast' observe: Mina hears Bramble’s exact parade promise. (3) 'inspect_books' observe: Mina discovers the uncollected readers’ books. (4) 'ask_route' tell: Mina tells Tuck where the readers are. (5) 'misread_judging' bridge: Tuck prepares the cart for a mayoral display when his belief names the mayor as judge. (6) 'choose_matched_books' pivotal beat: Mina loads books for particular readers, changing the bundle from tower to matched. (7) 'stack_high' beat: Tuck piles books high, changing cart.load_style to tower. (8) 'attach_bell' beat: Tuck attaches the brass bell. (9) 'ring_square' beat: the cart performs noisily at the town square, changing parade.kind to spectacle. (10) 'turn_to_homes' pivotal beat: Mina chooses the lane toward readers’ homes, changing cart.location and parade.kind to delivery. (11) 'deliver_first_book' beat: Mina gives a named reader’s book away, changing books.delivered and showing the parade’s purpose. (12) 'mayor_follows' bridge: Bramble follows, still expecting applause. (13) 'discover_empty_steps' observe: Bramble notices the square’s crowd is small while the homes have waiting readers. (14) 'ask_who_needs_books' tell: Bramble asks Mina and learns the reader list. (15) 'give_prize' beat: Bramble transfers the golden megaphone to Mina or Tuck, changing mayor.prize and mayor.agreement. (16) 'quiet_parade' ending beat: the bell is used softly at each doorstep, changing parade.kind to welcome. Include alternative guarded effects so the same loading, ringing, and following scenes lead to distinct outcomes: spectacle with towered books, useful delivery with matched books, or a reader-led welcome where Bramble abandons the biggest-parade boast. At least two scenes—'attach_bell' and 'mayor_follows'—must be reusable on materially different paths.","constraints":"Use 2–4 characters, one shared setting, and only the listed props. Every state key must begin with an existing entity ID such as mina, tuck, bramble, cart, books, sash, bell, or prize. Use at least observe, tell, or transfer; guard all knowledge-based actions so no character speaks from an unknown belief. Do not use counters, route numbers, or abstract popularity. The three problems must have different causes and consequences: (A) Bramble’s boast drives a noisy square spectacle that wins attention but leaves matched books undelivered; (B) Mina discovers that intended readers are waiting at home, conflicts with the mayor’s square plan, and creates a useful rolling delivery; (C) Tuck mistakes the judge and builds for display while Mina and Bramble discover that the true audience wants a gentle book welcome, leading to a small reader-led procession and a changed ownership or sharing of the prize. Goals should accept distinct concrete outcomes, such as parade.kind in ('spectacle','delivery','welcome'), books.delivered true, mayor.agreement true, and prize.owner in ('mina','tuck'). Mark only Mina’s reader-first choice and Bramble’s surrender of the boast as pivotal. No character should know a discovered fact before an observe or tell action.","different_endings":"1. Spectacle: The cart reaches the square stacked high, sash streaming and bell clanging. Bramble receives the golden megaphone, while the books remain bundled for another day; the final image is the mayor shouting into a prize far too large for his face. 2. Delivery: Mina turns the cart toward the waiting readers. Books leave the cart one by one, and Bramble gives up the golden megaphone so Tuck can use its handle to steady the red sash; the final image is a parade line of open books glowing in separate doorways. 3. Welcome: Tuck lowers the tower, Mina chooses a book for each listener, and Bramble agrees that a parade can be small if it arrives where it is wanted. The prize passes to the readers’ library shelf or to Mina, while the final image is the brass bell giving one soft chime as children wave from the steps. Provide at least two prose variants for each ending, with conditional wording tied to parade.kind, books.delivered, mayor.agreement, and prize.owner; never explain the lesson after the final image."}
